archetype.name: Point Guard (late-career)
archetype.definition: A 42-year-old distributor who wins on quick, short throws over the middle and to his tight ends, and who no longer threatens defenses vertically or escapes pressure the way he once did.

report.headline: Short game still works; deep shots, third downs and sacks are sinking him.
report.take:
Rodgers in 2026 is a quick-game quarterback attached to the league's best rushing offense. His intended air yards sit at 6.88 and he throws 1.92 yards short of the sticks on average. On throws of 0-9 air yards he is genuinely good: +0.144 EPA a play, +4.5 CPOE and nine of his 13 touchdowns. Between the numbers he is better still, +0.518 EPA on 64 middle-of-the-field attempts. His best receivers by efficiency are the two tight ends. Freiermuth (+0.228 per target) and Washington (+0.297) are the only top targets above zero, while DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard, who get the most volume, are both slightly negative.

The overall line is still poor: -0.095 EPA per dropback, 37th of 47 qualifiers and well below a league average of +0.034. Three things drag it down. The first is the deep ball, with 18.9% completions, a -16.6 CPOE and as many interceptions as touchdowns on 37 attempts. The second is third down, where he posts -0.363 EPA a play, converts 30.4% and has taken 15 of his 23 sacks. The third is sacks generally. His line keeps him clean (pressured on 19% of dropbacks, 11th-lowest of 38), but he converts pressure into sacks 37.3% of the time, 31st of 38. That is not new. His pressure-to-sack rate was 34.1% last year and 31.5% in 2024. Without the mobility to buy time, holding the ball (2.7 seconds, up from 2.59) turns into lost yardage.

The career line says this is a trend, not a slump. His EPA per play went from +0.058 with the Jets in 2024 to +0.064 last year to negative now, and his CPOE of -2.45 matches the -2.56 of 2024 rather than last year's neutral mark. The scheme puts a lot on him. Pittsburgh passes 3.3 points more than expected in neutral situations, fourth-most in the league, even though its run game ranks first in EPA and its passing game 28th. Under center, where play-action and the run threat help him, he is above water (+0.046 EPA). From shotgun he sits at -0.143.

The team keeps winning. A sixth-ranked defense and that run game carried a 3-0 stretch in Weeks 6-8 while his own efficiency fell to -0.138 per dropback. The fantasy value is real, at 233.9 yards a game (17th) and a pace17 of 28 touchdowns. But it rests on volume and red-zone finishing more than efficiency. Nine red-zone touchdowns have come with -0.238 EPA a play there.

strengths.title: Quick game over the middle
strengths.body: Under 10 air yards he completes 72.1% of short throws with a positive CPOE, and the middle of the field is his best area by a wide margin. Timing, anticipation and placement on short and intermediate throws have held up even as his arm and legs decline. This is the most durable part of his game.

strengths.title: Tight ends drive the passing game
strengths.body: Freiermuth and Washington are the only regular targets producing positive EPA, and both are clearly so. Their routes, seams and option work underneath fit his short-area accuracy, while the outside receivers have been break-even at best. As long as Pittsburgh keeps routing volume to the tight ends, the efficiency floor stays higher than the overall numbers suggest.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws hit big
strengths.body: He completes fewer than half his 10-19-yard throws, but the completions are chunk plays. They produce +0.307 EPA a play, more than his short game. That is a small sample of 48 attempts and partly the boom-or-bust nature of the depth. Still, it shows he can attack the second level when protection holds.

concerns.title: Sacks despite a clean pocket
concerns.body: Pressure is rare, but when it arrives he goes down more often than almost anyone. This is a three-year trait, not a blip, and it comes from a long-ish time to throw paired with very little scramble escape: just 4 scrambles all season. It is structural at his age and unlikely to improve.

concerns.title: Third downs are a disaster
concerns.body: On third down he is at -0.363 EPA a play with a 30.4% conversion rate and 15 sacks. An average of 7.5 yards to go, combined with a passer who throws short of the sticks, explains the poor conversion rate. The sack count shows defenses rushing hard in obvious passing downs. This is the single biggest drain on the season's EPA total.

concerns.title: Deep ball is gone
concerns.body: Fewer than one in five deep throws are completed, with a CPOE of -16.6 and three interceptions. Those picks drive his interception rate above last season's: 0.75 a game versus 0.44. With no WR producing positive EPA and Pittman on IR, there is little reason to expect this to turn. The fix is throwing deep less, not better.

trend.note: Weeks 3-5 were his best stretch, with positive EPA in all three and nine touchdowns. Weeks 6-8 slid to -0.138 EPA per dropback and a 2.9% TD rate, bottoming out at 13/25 with a -11 CPOE against Cleveland, even as Pittsburgh won all three.

nextGame.headline: Bengals' soft underneath defense suits him; their pass rush doesn't
nextGame.body:
Cincinnati fits his strengths. It ranks 27th in EPA allowed on short passes, which is exactly where Rodgers lives, but sixth on deep throws, which he should avoid anyway. It allows 289 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (30th) and gives tight ends 3.9 PPR points over their usual output (30th), with a larger-than-usual share of targets going to tight ends. The Bengals' offense ranks fourth in pass EPA and passes more than anyone over expectation. That could pull Pittsburgh into a higher-volume game, as in Week 3, when Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with +8.5 EPA against them. The catch is a sack rate tied for second-best in the league, a direct threat to his biggest weakness.

Pittsburgh comes off a bye with 14 days of rest. Michael Pittman Jr. (78% of snaps when healthy) carries a return estimate of the game date, but he said he has no clear timeline. Treat him as doubtful to help, which leaves the passing game leaning on the tight ends again. On Cincinnati's side, starting corner DJ Turner II (95% of snaps) is day-to-day with an ankle injury. His absence would soften the coverage on Metcalf. Edge rushers Cashius Howell and Cedric Johnson are also questionable, and thinning that rotation would matter given the Bengals' sack rate. Safety Kyle Dugger is out, but he is a part-timer.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: Cincinnati bleeds EPA on short throws, and Rodgers is efficient there. That should produce sustained drives and completions in volume. It is the clearest edge in the matchup.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends vs Bengals coverage
keyMatchups.body: The Bengals let top tight ends outscore their averages more than almost any defense, and Pittsburgh's tight ends are its only efficient targets. Expect Freiermuth and Washington to be the primary reads.

keyMatchups.title: Bengals pass rush on third down
keyMatchups.body: A top-two sack rate meets a quarterback who turns pressure into sacks at one of the league's highest rates, mostly on third down. If Pittsburgh's early downs leave long yardage, drives will die here.

nextGame.watch: Third-and-long: whether early-down runs keep him out of obvious passing situations against Cincinnati's pass rush.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should hold. Pittsburgh passes more than its situation calls for, its defense keeps games close, and the short game and tight-end usage are skills that have held up. Expect roughly 215-250 yards most weeks. The efficiency is unlikely to recover to last year's slightly positive level. The sack problem has been building for three seasons, the deep ball is broken, and the receivers outside the tight ends have not produced positive EPA. If anything, the red-zone touchdown rate, nine scores on a negative-EPA split, is the piece most likely to cool, so 1.2-1.8 touchdowns a game is the realistic band rather than the early-season peak.

The upside path is schematic. More under-center work off the league's top run game, where his EPA is positive, and fewer shotgun obvious-passing downs would cut both the sacks and the third-down losses. A Pittman return would also give him a third efficient target. The downside path is the Weeks 6-8 version continuing. In that version he stays a volume-driven QB2 who survives on yardage while interceptions run near one every game or so.
swingFactors: Share of dropbacks from under center

confidence.note: Eight games is a modest sample, but the decline matches a three-year career trend.
